doc.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023

title: Recording with Paul Simon
summary: Simon listened to each of 27 musicians individually, making sessions slow; the band played together from written parts.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: pieces in the thing. And he would go to every individual piece and listen what they were playing in, right next to you, he was standing right next to you while you’re playing. So a record, or a tune that would normally take twenty minutes would take three hours because we had a vast amount of musicians. And so it was more tedious than anything. But you know what? He produced great records all the time so that was his way of getting exactly what he wanted. And he would make these little changes and you’d do it and that’s it.
Would he make changes in things like the horn or the string parts? He’d like walk around and listen for something?

Yeah. He’d listen to everybody and suggest something or not suggest something. I can’t remember who, one of the arrangers — I would be guessing — but anyway that’s what he did. And his records were just marvelous records. They were just produced at a high level and you know I was there.
Were most of the — was most of the band there playing together or did you do a lot of overdubbing?
No together, together. I don’t know what happened after we got out of the studio but the band played together.
And because Paul, but Paul was a decent guitar player and —
So did you know what he was going to play? Was he playing it while you were playing? I guess my question is how did you fit your guitar playing into his strumming?

No the parts were written. There was hardly any, there was nothing improvised in his music for the guitar part. I don’t know, you know the players were pretty good. I’m sure that if somebody made a change that he would listen to it again to see if it was better than what he had envisioned. And you know I mean he had drummers like Steve Gadd and Grady Tate, you know if they envision something let’s hear it. If it works, fine. These are monster musicians so I’ll take some feedback from them any day.
